assertion: One release manifest per release correlates the whole tuple of the publish set and verifies every package, catalog, descriptor, evidence, and exception digest. Every package the release publishes is built from the release commit, and the first portfolio release publishes all four. A later release publishes only the packages whose version units changed. Each reused package keeps its original recorded version, digest, and provenance, and the manifest verifies its compatibility with the new tuple. It rejects repacked bytes under the same version, a package missing from the tuple, a newly published package built from another commit, and a reused package whose recorded digest or compatibility does not hold.
basis: E-P2.1-03 under the Roadmap P2.1 acceptance table, Decision 0032, and the P2.1 activation packet
command: npm-publish.yml dry run (main CI reused): pnpm generate && pnpm generate:check && node tooling/audits/repository-policy/src/release-prepare.mjs
npm-publish.yml mode=publish: promote the dry run's npm-candidate artifact, then publish the set in order (npm-publication.mjs publish-set)
published tuple (E-P2.1-02): pnpm install --ignore-scripts --no-frozen-lockfile --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ in a clean project, then the installed muxui bin
prior tuple (E-P2.1-06): pnpm install --ignore-scripts --no-frozen-lockfile --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ in a clean project, then the installed muxui bin once (manifest --json)

disclosureBasis: Public reproducibility class (Architecture, "Evidence also carries a disclosure class"): sanitized log excerpts, digests, and registry read-backs of public packages. No consumer code, prompts, screens, or traces were captured, so SCOPE-TRUST-EVIDENCE-PRIVACY is not applicable to P2.1.
expiry: Retained as P2.1 proof for this exact release; a later release needs new E-P2.1 evidence rather than an edit

independentReview.required: an independent reviewer of a different model and harness from the authoring agents, bound to the reviewed revision (P2.1 activation packet, "Roles")

limits: Reuse is shown by one real preparation, this release's, against the one prior release (muxui-portfolio:40dcc0032b7db3a47e19797d4e73bc9d). A reuse chain, where a package the prior release itself reused is reused again, has not occurred in a real release and is modeled by fixtures only.

The repeated-preparation digest is shown by the fixture test. The dry run prepared this commit once, and the publish run promoted its candidate instead of preparing again, so no second real preparation is retained.
nonClaims: P2.1 is not claimed complete, ready, or exited by this record; the exit condition is judged from the Roadmap, not from this root.
No stable release, support, or assistive-technology claim. Install guidance for these packages uses @next.
latest is observed, not claimed or promoted: this release published @muxui/tooling to next and left latest where the first release's read-back saw it for every package (Decision 0023).

@muxui/schema and @muxui/catalog: Andrew reported setting up their trusted publishers on npm. That is not observable from public data, no publish has used them, and tokenless publishing stays unproved for those two. As given to this capture, npm's documentation says a trusted publisher that goes unused lapses after 2 days; this capture did not read that documentation. @muxui/tooling's publish by trusted publishing (OIDC) is the observation in E-P2.1-06; @muxui/react's is the first release's.

@muxui/schema, @muxui/catalog, and @muxui/tooling each also list a 0.0.0-stage placeholder version. It is no part of the release tuple, carries no provenance, and is not claimed; npm most likely created it, which is inferred and not proved.
Recovery is prepared, not exercised. This release shows that the first release's tuple stays installable and verifiable by exact version; restoring a prior tuple stays owed by P2 exit.
No consumer validation, clean-consumer offline proof, docs, explorer, or MCP evidence (P2.2 and P2.3).
